defects.claim: AXIS 1 FAILS — the id-keyed census is still open. A fresh re-derivation over the 92-record corpus (231 *.md non-recursive = 58 kf + 66 fr + 15 pt + 92 corpus; 233 files incl. delta-r3's 2 worker files — §0's dated correction verifies) finds 3,059 bold-leading rows, of which 1,290 carry an X-W token (hyphen and dotted forms; NO en-dash form exists in the corpus — `grep 'X–W|X—W|X‑W'` = 0) and 321 carry NO-WAVE-OWNER on the row line. Testing each ⟨record·id⟩ against the ENTIRE fold layer (12 folds + spine + ROUND-1-ASSIGNMENTS) under its own record namespace leaves **84 distinct ⟨record·id⟩ across 27 records absent by bytes**, none of them in any exclusion register and none 'excluded-with-reason'. The escapes are not marginal: seven of them are X-W4-routed rows in one record that X-W4-FOLD §6B claims to have closed, and six are X-W7-routed rows in a record X-W7-FOLD §R1.16 folds as complete. Root cause is method, not oversight: X-W7-FOLD's own §R1 method requires the wave token 'within 30 characters after a routing marker (→ · Disposition · BUILD · BOOK · Terminal · routes to · re-homed · rides · owns/owner · | **)', so rows routed by bare declarative phrasing — '**X-W7 rider else boundary.**', 'X-W7 ride', 'carried in the X-W4 family', 'dies whole with **X-W7.d**' — are invisible to every seat that inherited it.
